title: Agree who clears up
description: Agree who clears up after a shared task, before the task ends.
oneStarDescription: Ask who will clear up before everyone is tired.
twoStarDescription: Agree a split or one person, in a sentence.
threeStarDescription: Do the part you took, and say if you cannot.

title: Apologize and offer a repair
description: Apologize for a specific act and offer a repair the other person can accept or refuse.
oneStarDescription: Say what you did, without adding their motive.
twoStarDescription: Offer one concrete repair.
threeStarDescription: If they refuse or want something else, accept that answer and do not insist.

title: Set a blanket out of the path
description: Set a blanket where people can still pass, and pack it up.
oneStarDescription: Choose a spot that is not on a path or in front of an exit.
twoStarDescription: Set the blanket and keep bags on it.
threeStarDescription: Pack everything you brought and look once for anything left.

title: Ask where to start in a gallery
description: Ask a guard or a desk where to start, and follow or adapt their answer.
oneStarDescription: Ask where a first-time visitor should start.
twoStarDescription: Go to the place they name, or say why you are choosing a different start.
threeStarDescription: Thank them and do not keep them from other visitors.

title: Ask before you touch a display
description: Ask whether a display may be touched, and keep your hands off until the answer is yes.
oneStarDescription: Look for a touch or do-not-touch sign.
twoStarDescription: If there is no sign, ask a staff member.
threeStarDescription: Touch only after a yes, and describe what you were allowed to touch.

title: Ask for a dissent
description: Ask whether anyone sees the decision differently, and record that view.
oneStarDescription: After a proposal, ask if anyone disagrees or is unsure.
twoStarDescription: Write the dissenting point without arguing it down in the same breath.
threeStarDescription: Say whether the decision changed, or that it stood and the dissent remains noted.

title: Ask for a pause
description: Ask to pause a conversation and say when you can return.
oneStarDescription: Ask for a pause in one sentence.
twoStarDescription: Say when you will come back, or that you cannot name a time yet.
threeStarDescription: Return at that time, or send an update if you cannot.

title: Ask for a story and write it down
description: Ask one prepared question about a memory, write the answer, and check it with the teller.
oneStarDescription: Ask a question you prepared, and let the person answer.
twoStarDescription: Write the answer and mark anything you were unsure you heard.
threeStarDescription: Read it back and change what they say is wrong. Do not share it unless they agree.

title: Balance a hanging mobile
description: Hang two objects so a stick hangs level.
oneStarDescription: Suspend a stick from one point and see which side drops.
twoStarDescription: Move an object or add a small one until the stick hangs level.
threeStarDescription: Move one object, show the tilt, and restore the level.

title: Be heard at the back of a room
description: Speak so a person at the back can repeat your sentence, without straining.
oneStarDescription: Speak one sentence to a person at the back of the room.
twoStarDescription: Ask them to repeat it, and try once more if they missed a word.
threeStarDescription: If your throat tightens, stop and say you would rest rather than push.

title: Darken a room for a viewing
description: Darken a room enough to see a screen or a projection, and restore the light after.
oneStarDescription: Close blinds or switch off lights until the image is visible.
twoStarDescription: Leave enough light to see the way to the door, or say you cannot and stop.
threeStarDescription: Put the room back when the viewing ends.

title: Borrow a library item and note the due date
description: Borrow an item and record when it is due, then return or renew it.
oneStarDescription: Borrow an item on your own account.
twoStarDescription: Write the due date where you will see it.
threeStarDescription: Return it or renew it before the date, and keep the new receipt if you renew.

title: Bounce light with a mirror
description: Use a mirror to send a patch of light to a target you chose.
oneStarDescription: Use a mirror to put a patch of daylight or a lamp on a wall.
twoStarDescription: Move the mirror until the patch sits on a target you marked.
threeStarDescription: Say what happens when the light source is blocked, and do not claim a rule about lasers.

title: Build a den that leaves the exit clear
description: Build a temporary den from chairs and cloth that does not block the way out.
oneStarDescription: Point to the door and build so the path to it stays open.
twoStarDescription: Arrange cloth and chairs so the den stands when you are inside.
threeStarDescription: Take it down and put the chairs back.

title: Build a glossary for a topic
description: Collect words for one topic, each with a meaning in your own words.
oneStarDescription: Choose one topic and write several words with meanings you could explain aloud.
twoStarDescription: Use one of the words in a sentence about a real source you read.
threeStarDescription: If two entries overlap, merge them or say how they differ.

title: Bundle cables and label them
description: Bundle cables you may touch and label what each one serves.
oneStarDescription: If a cable is safe to unplug, unplug it before you bundle, or leave it if you are not sure.
twoStarDescription: Bundle one cable and label the device it serves.
threeStarDescription: Follow the label to the device and correct the label if it is wrong.

title: Call a cue for someone else
description: Give a cue at the agreed moment and not early.
oneStarDescription: Mark the word or action that triggers the cue.
twoStarDescription: Give the cue at that moment, loud enough for the person who needs it.
threeStarDescription: If you were early or late, mark the script and say how you will watch the next time.

title: Caption a short clip
description: Add words to a short clip so a viewer can read what is said.
oneStarDescription: Write the spoken words of a few seconds you are allowed to caption.
twoStarDescription: Show the words while those sounds are heard, not after the clip has moved on.
threeStarDescription: Add one non-speech sound that matters, such as a door, or say there was none.

title: Carry a load close to you
description: Carry a moderate load close to your body and put it down if the path is unclear.
oneStarDescription: Pick up a box you can manage and hold it against your torso.
twoStarDescription: Walk only where you can see the floor, and stop if you cannot.
threeStarDescription: Put the load down or set it aside to open a door, rather than forcing it.

title: Check a doorway with a tape
description: Measure a doorway and compare it with a width you were asked about.
oneStarDescription: Measure the clear width of a doorway with a tape, in the unit you were asked for.
twoStarDescription: Compare the number with the width you were given and say which is larger.
threeStarDescription: Note a threshold or a door swing that the number alone does not show.

title: Check a link before you share it
description: Open a link yourself and say what the page is before you send it on.
oneStarDescription: Open the link and read the title of the page.
twoStarDescription: Write one sentence on what the page actually is.
threeStarDescription: Share it only if it matches what you meant to send, and say so if you stop.

title: Check a sale price
description: Work out a sale price from the original and the discount, and compare it with the tag.
oneStarDescription: Point to the original price and the discount on a tag or a sign.
twoStarDescription: Compute the sale price and show the arithmetic.
threeStarDescription: Compare your result with the price charged, and say whether they match.

title: Check whether a sign can be read
description: Look at a sign and say whether the words can be read from the place a person would stand.
oneStarDescription: Stand where a reader would stand and read the sign aloud, or say which word you cannot read.
twoStarDescription: Say whether the problem is size, contrast, glare, or something in the way.
threeStarDescription: Propose one change, such as a darker pen or a move out of the glare, and show a version you can read.

title: Choose a book by its blurb and check the opening
description: Choose a book from the blurb, then check the opening and say if the blurb matched.
oneStarDescription: Read the blurb and say what you expect the book to be.
twoStarDescription: Read the opening page before you decide the book matches the blurb.
threeStarDescription: Say one way the opening matches or breaks the blurb.

title: Choose a meeting spot if you get separated
description: Agree a meeting spot before you enter a crowded place.
oneStarDescription: Name a spot you can both find, such as a specific door.
twoStarDescription: Say how long you will wait there before you use a phone.
threeStarDescription: If you do get separated, go there, or if you do not, say the plan stayed unused.

title: Choose a size people can read
description: Set type or lettering large enough for the reader you have in mind.
oneStarDescription: Say who will read it and from how far.
twoStarDescription: Make two sizes and ask that reader, or someone standing in for them, which they can read.
threeStarDescription: Use the size they could read, and say if a longer text still will not fit.

title: Choose a seat you can leave
description: Choose a seat you can leave without climbing over people, when you have a choice.
oneStarDescription: Look at the path from a free seat to the aisle.
twoStarDescription: Sit in a seat with a clear path, or say there is no such seat and you will stand or wait.
threeStarDescription: Leave by that path when you need to, without a new disturbance you could avoid.

title: Clap along and stop when you lose it
description: Clap along with music and stop when you are no longer with it, then say where you lost it.
oneStarDescription: Clap with a recording for a short stretch.
twoStarDescription: Stop when you notice you are off, instead of hiding it.
threeStarDescription: Say or replay the moment you lost the beat.

title: Clap the stresses of a word
description: Clap the stressed beats of a word or a short line.
oneStarDescription: Clap the louder beat of a word with more than one beat.
twoStarDescription: Clap the stresses of a short line you can see.
threeStarDescription: Say how the line would sound if the stress moved, and clap that version once.

title: Clear a work surface
description: Clear a surface so the task has room, and put the cleared things where you can find them.
oneStarDescription: Take off the items the next task does not use.
twoStarDescription: Put those items in one place you can name.
threeStarDescription: Start the task on the clear surface, and say if you still lack room.

title: Close a conversation
description: End a conversation so the other person knows it is ending.
oneStarDescription: Say that you need to stop, in a sentence.
twoStarDescription: Say the next step, or that there is none.
threeStarDescription: Leave or let them leave, without starting a new topic.

title: Cluster a list of ideas
description: Group a list of ideas by similarity and name each group.
oneStarDescription: Put ideas that belong together into piles, and leave one aside if it fits nowhere.
twoStarDescription: Give each pile a name the group can accept.
threeStarDescription: Split a pile that hides two topics, or merge two piles that are the same, and say which you did.

title: Coil a cable without a kink
description: Coil a cable so it lies in loops and uncoils without a knot.
oneStarDescription: Coil the cable into loops of similar size.
twoStarDescription: Fasten the coil with a strap or the cable's own end so it stays.
threeStarDescription: Uncoil it and show that it does not come out in a knot.

title: Collect questions before a talk
description: Collect questions before a talk so the speaker sees them in time.
oneStarDescription: Ask the group for questions before the talk starts.
twoStarDescription: Put two similar questions together and keep both names if they want.
threeStarDescription: Give the list to the speaker and say which question you did not understand well enough to group.

title: Color-code a shared calendar
description: Agree what calendar colors mean and use them on one week.
oneStarDescription: Agree what two colors mean with the other person.
twoStarDescription: Color one week using only those meanings.
threeStarDescription: If a color was used for two things, change one and tell the other person.

title: Compare a headline with the text
description: Compare a headline with the first part of the article and say what the headline added or left out.
oneStarDescription: Read the headline and the opening of the article.
twoStarDescription: Name one claim in the headline that the opening does or does not support.
threeStarDescription: Write a plainer headline that matches the opening, and mark it as yours.

title: Compare how cups hold heat
description: Compare two cups of warm water and say which stays warmer, without a medical claim.
oneStarDescription: Pour the same warm water into two different cups and note the time.
twoStarDescription: After the same wait, feel or measure both and say which is warmer.
threeStarDescription: Name one way the test was not fair, such as a different amount or a draft.

title: Compare two objects in a gallery
description: Compare two objects using what you can see and what their labels say.
oneStarDescription: Choose two objects and say one visible difference.
twoStarDescription: Add one difference that comes from the labels, such as date or place.
threeStarDescription: Write one comparison you cannot settle from the objects and the labels.

title: Compare two leaf edges
description: Compare the edges of two leaves and say how they differ.
oneStarDescription: Take two fallen leaves or look at two you do not pick, and lay the comparison out.
twoStarDescription: Say how the edges differ, using words such as smooth, toothed, or lobed.
threeStarDescription: Say you have not named the plants, unless a guide you can show confirms them.

title: Compare two ramps
description: Roll the same object down two ramps and say which was faster or farther.
oneStarDescription: Roll the same object down one ramp and mark where it stops.
twoStarDescription: Change the height or the surface, roll again, and say what changed.
threeStarDescription: Repeat the better trial and say whether the result held.
